related_questions.question: What is the best thing to take for COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: For mild COVID-19, symptom relief can be achieved with over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen. Rest, hydration, and monitoring symptoms are also crucial. High-risk individuals may be eligible for prescription medications to prevent severe illness.

list.snippet: Fever reducers/pain relievers: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) can help manage fever and body aches.
Cough suppressants: Cough syrups or medications can help relieve coughing fits.
Other symptom relief: Nasal decongestants or throat lozenges may also be helpful depending on the symptoms.
Individuals at high risk of severe COVID-19 illness may be eligible for prescription antiviral medications like Paxlovid. These medications can help prevent mild illness from worsening.
High-risk individuals include those 65 and older, those with certain medical conditions, and those with weakened immune systems.
Rest and Hydration: Resting and drinking plenty of fluids are essential for recovery.
Monitoring Symptoms: If symptoms worsen or become severe, seek medical advice.
Isolation: If you have COVID-19, isolate yourself from others to prevent spreading the virus.
Consult your doctor: Consult with a healthcare professional for personalized advice on managing COVID-19.

related_questions.question: How to recover from COVID faster?

text_blocks.snippet: To recover from COVID-19 faster, focus on getting plenty of rest, staying hydrated, and managing symptoms with over-the-counter medications. Vaccination can also help reduce the severity and duration of symptoms. Additionally, maintaining good hygiene practices, like wearing a mask and not sharing items, can prevent further spread and potentially aid in a quicker recovery.
snippet_highlighted_words: focus on getting plenty of rest, staying hydrated, and managing symptoms with over-the-counter medications

list.title: Rest:
list.snippet: Allow your body ample time to recover by getting sufficient sleep, ideally more than the recommended 7-9 hours for adults.

list.title: Hydration:
list.snippet: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, which can help with overall recovery and symptom management.

list.title: Symptom Management:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help alleviate fever and body aches.

list.title: Vaccination:
list.snippet: Vaccination can significantly reduce the severity and duration of COVID-19 symptoms.

list.title: Hygiene:
list.snippet: Wear a mask when around others, avoid sharing personal items, and maintain good hand hygiene to prevent further spread.

list.title: Monitor Symptoms:
list.snippet: Keep a close watch on your symptoms and seek medical attention if you experience severe symptoms or if your condition worsens.

related_questions.question: How long does it take to get over COVID?
related_questions.snippet: Early research suggested that it could take two weeks for your body to get over a mild illness or up to six weeks for severe or critical cases. Recovery varies for different people, depending on things like your age and overall health. Fatigue, headache, and troubled breathing are the symptoms most likely to linger.

list.snippet: Most people with mild COVID-19 can recover at home with rest, hydration, and over-the-counter medications like acetaminophen or ibuprofen.
If you have severe symptoms, such as difficulty breathing, chest pain, or confusion, seek immediate medical attention.
Some antiviral medications may be available for high-risk individuals.
If you test positive for COVID-19, isolate yourself at home for at least 5 days.
Wear a mask around others and avoid close contact.
Quarantine household members who may have been exposed.
Monitor your symptoms and contact your healthcare provider if they worsen or new symptoms develop.
Get tested again if you need to leave isolation.
Inform your employer and school about your diagnosis.
Follow local public health guidelines.
Stay up-to-date on the latest information from the CDC or WHO.

text_blocks.snippet: Remember: The best way to protect yourself and others from COVID-19 is to get vaccinated and follow preventive measures. If you test positive, follow isolation and quarantine guidelines to prevent further spread.
